newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rebound on industrial data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rebound on industrial data.

text.p: Mexican stocks rebounded from their earlier dip to re-enter positive territory at mid-morning trade on Tuesday. Dealers said strong industrial output data triggered the recovery in share prices.

"Buyers stepped back in after the industrial activity data were released. The prepayment announcement and the Dow helped, of course, but the real detonator was the industrial data," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 8.55 points, or 0.21 percent, at 4,268.56.

Mexico's Finance Ministry announced industrial activity in April rose by 15 percent compared to the same month last year. A Reuters survey of 13 financial firms showed they had forecast an average increase of 7.92 percent before the data.
Dealers noted the data came as a welcome sign that a much-heralded economic recovery could be under way.

The Finance Ministry also announced a debt refinancing package for Mexico, including a decision to prepay $6 billion in floating-rate bank notes and the issue of $1 billion in five-year floating-rate bonds.
The Dow Jones had also recovered from an early slide, and was up 16.78 points at 7,788.82.
"The buyers are back, and the floor is in full cry again," the floor trader added. "There's no overall trend, they're buying across the board."
Dealing .TV.MX was brisk, although dealers noted three hefty cross trades had inflated a total of 68.1 million shares traded.
Traders said heavyweight Telmex had done most to turn the market around. The telecomms stock was up 14 centavos to 18.86 pesos, and had earlier traded as low as 18.60 pesos.
The IPC had earlier climbed as high as 4,287.44 points. Brisk trading volume .TV.MX of 145.2 million reflected the strong presence of foreign investors, dealers said.
Mexico's Finance Ministry (Hacienda) announced during early trade that industrial activity in April had risen by 15 percent compared to the same month in 1996.
The figure far outpaced an average rise of 7.92 percent forecast in a Reuters survey of 13 financial firms MEX22.
Hacienda also announced the government would prepay an entire $6 billion issue of floating-rate bank notes placed Aug. 5, 1996.
Telmex ADRs were meanwhile up 1/8 to 47-1/2.
Dealers said financial group Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest, was also driving the bourse, but had been firm all morning on demand from foreign brokers.
Bancomer was up 7 centavos at 3.87 pesos.
On the broad market, a total of 86 stocks had changed hands, of which gainers outpaced sliders by 43 to 25.
